title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
problem: Large language models study reasoning (e.g., chain-of-thought) and acting (action plan generation) separately, which limits their ability to interact with environments, handle exceptions, update plans, or avoid hallucination and error propagation.
method: ReAct, a prompt-based paradigm that interleaves verbal reasoning traces (thoughts) and task-specific actions, allowing the model to perform dynamic reasoning and interface with external environments (e.g., Wikipedia API, web navigation, text-based games).
key_results: ReAct outperforms acting-only and reasoning-only baselines on diverse language and decision-making tasks, improving absolute success rates by 34% on ALFWorld and 10% on WebShop compared to imitation/reinforcement learning methods, while reducing hallucinations.
limitations: The unlimited language space makes learning difficult without strong language priors; interleaving reasoning and action can reduce flexibility and cause repetitive loops under greedy decoding.
future_work: Scaling up ReAct with multi-task training, combining with reinforcement learning, and exploring better decoding strategies like beam search.
key_claims: Interleaving reasoning and acting allows greater synergy, where reasoning helps track and update plans and actions gather external information.
ReAct overcomes prevalent issues of hallucination and error propagation found in chain-of-thought reasoning.
ReAct significantly outperforms existing imitation and reinforcement learning baselines on interactive decision-making benchmarks with minimal in-context examples.
Combining reasoning and acting provides better model interpretability, trustworthiness, and diagnosability.
